Docs/Replay/Guide

Replay

Combat feedback

1 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓

Hit/dash/pickup bursts, layered death/blast bursts, debris, enemy damage numbers and pickup/healing text now live in bounded presentation pools. Journal effects use Replay's one-shot ledger; enemy numbers use each target's observed HP loss and generation/tick identity. No simulation or checkpoint fields are added.

Confirmation/update does not restart an effect. Cancellation removes only the matching identity; epoch/resync and floor/run changes clear old views. Initial or restored enemy observations seed silently. Damage numbers can combine changes between observations; pickup/heal totals follow the existing aggregated events.

The original 12-particle bursts and floating-text motion supply the basic look. The pools cap burst/text/debris nodes at 256/128/256, with counted overflow. Their lifetimes are 0.8/0.9/0.55 seconds respectively. These bounds limit visuals, not gameplay damage or drops.

Shell
nix develop --command bash examples/replay_scrapyard/feedback_run.sh
RSY_HEADED_HOST=1 RSY_AUDIO_DRIVER=Dummy \
  RSY_FEEDBACK_CAPTURE=/absolute/existing/output/directory \
  nix develop --command bash examples/replay_scrapyard/feedback_run.sh

Evidence covers live damage/pickup, expiry, floor changes, faulted stress and recovery. The frame timer now includes deferred feedback/audio/social upkeep; older measurements used a narrower scope. Native captures use Dummy audio, and WASM is compile-checked. Broader browser visuals, hardware listening, playtests and full comparison remain requirements.

Screen effects now restore lens kicks, vignette and transition veil.

Directional wounds now use recorded geometry and correct the hurt burst's placement at the victim rather than the origin.

Wall contacts now add confirmed ballistic/spit sparks from exact collision endpoints and normals; terminal expiry and body hits do not invent wall effects.
